episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator
question: What is the back end of a challenge in online marketing?
transcript_excerpt: The back end of a challenge refers to the transformation and next offer step after the challenge concludes. At the end of a challenge, participants are invited to take the next step, which could look different for different people—you might go to a membership, purchase a course, or join a coaching program. The challenge itself is a time-based online event where you give participants bite-sized daily lessons focused on one thing, building know, like, and trust so they fall in love with you before presenting that back-end offer.

episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator
question: How did Pedro Adeo make seven figures on the back end of challenges?
transcript_excerpt: Pedro Adeo was one of the first online marketers to make seven figures on the back end of a challenge, which at the time was completely unheard of. He took the challenge model that Russell Brunson had already been running, tweaked it, and made it better. This success got Russell Brunson's attention and things blew up overnight. Alyssa was his designer during this period and witnessed challenges being run with high-profile figures like Damon John from Shark Tank, Grant Cardone, Tony Robbins, Dean Graziosi, and Lisa Nichols.

episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator
question: Why was Alyssa Aviles rejected from the university graphic design program?
transcript_excerpt: Alyssa applied for the graphic design program at her university but was denied entry. The school told her that her work sucked. She had spent two years in art classes preparing for the program, but the school judged her based on traditional art work rather than graphic design, so they didn't have a chance to see any of the graphic design work she was actually creating on her own.

episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator
question: What design mistake did Pedro Adeo make on his original funnel page?
transcript_excerpt: Pedro's original funnel page was a white blank page with just a logo he had made for 100X in a font style, a photo of him, and all the copy was written in a font called Caveat Brush, which Alyssa noted is not good for screens and not legible at all. Alyssa thought it was not appealing visually, though she was impressed by the actual copy writing itself.

episode_title: Alyssa Aviles / Creative Growth Partner & Design Educator
question: How much did Alyssa charge for her first wedding photography shoot?
transcript_excerpt: Alyssa shot her very first wedding for $125. A trumpet player she had met at a jazz night at the coffee shop where she worked asked her to shoot his wedding even though she had never shot a wedding before. He told her he loved who she was, saw value in what she did, and wanted to pay her. This was the moment that showed her photography could be a career and service she could offer to other people.
